clue.text: Meet outside the food shop — that's the start of your devotion

indicators.note: the word for meet sits outside the shop, wrapping round it

parts.note: meet in the sense of suitable or proper gives fit
a deli is a delicatessen, a shop selling prepared foods

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the following word is wanted

explanation.surface: Someone waits outside the delicatessen as a first sign of their loyalty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Meet' looks like a verb but is the old adjective meaning fitting; 'outside' makes it wrap round the shop, and 'the start of' your adds the last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Faithfulness and loyal attachment to a person or cause are what devotion and this word both name.

indicators.note: the slang cigarette goes round the Roman numeral, enclosing it

parts.note: fag is British slang for a cigarette, a smoke
L is the Roman numeral for fifty
on, as in on board, means aboard

explanation.surface: Someone lights a cigarette near fifty passengers on board a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' makes the British slang word for a cigarette wrap round the Roman fifty.
explanation.definitionFit: A flagon is a large container for wine or cider, a vessel in the sense of a container for liquid.

clue.text: One who would be king's trendy artistic ability

parts.note: a draughtsman is a piece in the game of draughts (checkers), which is crowned king on reaching the far side; the possessive gives the S
hip means fashionable, trendy

explanation.surface: Seems to describe a fashionable heir to the throne's talent for the arts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One who would be king' looks like a royal heir, but it is a draughts piece hoping to be crowned on the back row; draughts is the British name for checkers.
explanation.definitionFit: Skill at drawing plans and pictures is a form of artistic ability.

clue.text: Permissible but to some extent duplicitous

indicators.note: only a portion of the following word is used, the run inside it

explanation.surface: Something is allowed yet a little deceitful.
explanation.definitionFit: Licit is the formal word for lawful or allowed, the opposite of illicit.

parts.note: T is the grammar abbreviation for tense
a rigger erects scaffolding or rigging on building sites

explanation.surface: A nervous builder starts something going.
explanation.definitionFit: To trigger an event is to set it off, start it happening.

indicators.note: corrupted means spoilt or altered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Women's ethics have been led astray.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corrupted' rearranges LADIES.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideals are the moral principles or standards a person lives by, as morals are.

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the deer surround the organ meat

parts.note: does are female deer, so the plural deer stands in for them
liver is a kind of offal, edible internal organs

explanation.surface: A rescuer manages without eating innards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'does' reads as a verb but is the plural of doe; 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, so the animals surround the organ.
explanation.definitionFit: A deliverer sets people free from danger, so is a rescuer or saviour.

clue.text: Out of character but not for a malt whisky drinker

definitions.meaning: doing something contrary to one's nature

definitions.text: not for a malt whisky drinker
definitions.meaning: a malt whisky drinker would oppose grain whisky, made from grains other than malted barley

explanation.walkthrough: Malt whisky is made only from malted barley, while grain whisky is made from other cereals, so a malt purist is literally opposed to grain.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means contrary to one's natural inclination, and literally describes someone who dislikes grain whisky.

indicators.note: only the first half of the word is finished, so its first three letters are kept

parts.note: let on means revealed or disclosed a secret

explanation.surface: A half-finished drawing showed the basic shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half complete' keeps SKE, the first half of SKETCH.
explanation.definitionFit: A skeleton is the bare framework of something, its basic outline.

clue.text: An artist turned fashionable and rebellious

indicators.note: turned means turned round, so the two letters are read backwards

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, the usual crossword artist
chic means stylish, fashionable

explanation.surface: A painter changed into someone stylish and defiant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' reverses RA to AR.
explanation.definitionFit: Anarchic means without order or control, rejecting authority, so rebellious in spirit.

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for parking on road signs
a lease is a contract to rent property, an agreement

explanation.surface: Seems to ask a landlord to approve a deal for a parking space.
explanation.definitionFit: To please someone is to satisfy or gratify them.

clue.text: Drink up! The end of the earth is at hand

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word is written bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: gin is an alcoholic drink

indicators.note: only the final letter of the next word is taken

explanation.surface: A drinking toast: drink up, for the end of the world is coming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses GIN to NIG in this down entry, and 'The end of' earth gives H.
explanation.definitionFit: Nigh is an old word for near, so close at hand.

indicators.note: the word loses its opening letter, its introduction

parts.note: sought means looked for, pursued

explanation.surface: Seems to say something ought to be chased without being presented first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without introduction' drops the S of SOUGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: Ought expresses obligation, used in the same way as should.

indicators.note: making signals the letters of the two words are worked into something new

explanation.surface: A man named Vince gets angry, which causes resentment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making' rearranges VINCE and RAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A grievance is resentment over a perceived wrong, a bad feeling held against someone.

indicators.note: developed means changed or worked into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The French novelist Marcel Proust became sluggish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developed' rearranges PROUST.
explanation.definitionFit: A stupor is a dazed state of near unconsciousness, a deep lethargy.

parts.note: P is piano, the musical marking for quiet
re means about or concerning
a tender is a formal offer, as in a bid for a contract

explanation.surface: A claimant keeps silent about a bid.
explanation.definitionFit: A pretender is someone who claims a throne or title, so a claimant.

parts.note: a ratio is the relationship between two quantities

explanation.surface: A Shakespearean actor's husband has a long-standing relationship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'relationship' looks romantic but is the mathematical one, a ratio.
explanation.definitionFit: Horatio is Hamlet's loyal friend in Shakespeare's play, so a Shakespearean character.

clue.text: British rugby player's lifetime of obstruction

parts.note: a lock is a second-row forward in rugby
an age is a lifetime, a long span of years

explanation.surface: A British rugby player's whole career is spent in a blocked position.
explanation.walkthrough: A lock is a rugby forward in the second row of the scrum.
explanation.definitionFit: A blockage is something that obstructs, as in a blocked pipe.

parts.note: lam is informal for hit hard, thrash
Lizzie and Beth are both short forms of Elizabeth

explanation.surface: Someone strikes a girl named Lizzie inside a royal residence.
explanation.walkthrough: Lambeth Palace is the London residence of the Archbishop of Canterbury.
explanation.definitionFit: Lambeth Palace in London is the official home of the Archbishop of Canterbury.

clue.text: A section in Westminster requires fastening

indicators.note: the article and the abbreviation go inside the two letters for parliament

parts.note: HP stands for Houses of Parliament, which sit at Westminster

explanation.surface: A clause in a parliamentary act calls for something to be fastened.
explanation.walkthrough: Westminster is the London seat of the Houses of Parliament, abbreviated HP; A and S go inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A hasp is a hinged metal clasp fitting over a staple, closed with a padlock, so a fastening.

clue.text: Ruin quiet locality ultimately like Slough

parts.note: to mar is to spoil or ruin
sh is a call for quiet

indicators.note: ultimately points to the last letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Seems to describe spoiling a peaceful neighbourhood, like the English town of Slough.
explanation.walkthrough: Slough is a town west of London, but here the capital is only for the surface: a slough is a bog.
explanation.definitionFit: A slough is a swamp or bog, so being like one means boggy and wet.

clue.text: Formed separatist group in Atlantic territory

parts.note: made means formed or created
the IRA, the Irish Republican Army, fought for Irish unity separate from Britain

explanation.surface: A breakaway group set up on an island in the Atlantic.
explanation.definitionFit: Madeira is a Portuguese island group in the Atlantic Ocean, an autonomous region.

indicators.note: excitedly suggests agitation, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Hurry eagerly to the capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excitedly' rearranges HASTEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Athens is the capital city of Greece.

indicators.note: the prisoner comes first, before the word for skilled

parts.note: con is short for convict, a prisoner
versed means experienced or skilled in something

explanation.surface: Someone talked to a skilled inmate before anyone else.
explanation.definitionFit: To converse is to talk, so having conversed is having spoken with someone.

parts.note: Ar is an abbreviation for Arab or Arabic
got means obtained, picked up

explanation.surface: An Arab learned the local language.
explanation.definitionFit: Argot is the slang or jargon of a group, its vernacular.

clue.text: Period with conservationists is a factor

parts.note: an age is a period of time
NT is the National Trust, the British conservation charity

explanation.surface: An era when conservationists play a part.
explanation.walkthrough: The National Trust is a British charity that looks after historic houses and countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: A factor and an agent are both people who act for another in business.

clue.text: A clergyman suppressed initial story of pests

parts.note: P is an abbreviation for priest, a clergyman
hid means concealed, suppressed

indicators.note: initial points to the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A priest kept quiet about the first account of an infestation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initial' takes S from story.
explanation.definitionFit: Aphids are greenflies and other tiny sap-sucking insects, garden pests.

clue.text: Free bishop trapped in seedy atelier

indicators.note: the bishop is held inside the rearranged letters
seedy means shabby or run-down, so the letters are disordered

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: Release a churchman held captive in a shabby studio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seedy' rearranges ATELIER to LIERATE, and 'trapped in' puts B inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To liberate is to set free, release.

clue.text: Great power of representative in republic

indicators.note: the representative sits inside the name of the republic

parts.note: Eire is the Irish name for the Republic of Ireland
an MP, Member of Parliament, is an elected representative

explanation.surface: Seems to ask about a great power held by a politician in a republic.
explanation.walkthrough: Eire is the Irish-language name for the Republic of Ireland; 'in' seats the politician inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An empire is a large realm under one ruler, a great power among nations.

parts.note: HA is an abbreviation for heavy artillery
stings means hurts sharply

explanation.surface: Big guns cause pain in a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: The Battle of Hastings in 1066 was where William of Normandy defeated the English king Harold.
explanation.definitionFit: Hastings is the 1066 battle in which the Normans conquered England.
